Bug_Details:
Optional acts as a container object that may or may not contain a non-null value. It is introduced in Java 8 to help avoid NullPointerException . It provides methods to check if a value is present and retrieve the value if it is present.
Optional is used instead of null values to make the code more readable and avoid potential errors.
It is a bad practice to use null with Optional because it is unclear whether a value is present or not, leading to
confusion and potential NullPointerException errors.
Bug_Explanation: The `showBug` method first creates an Optional of an Integer using `Optional.ofNullable(null)`. When `orElse` method is called on this Optional, it returns the value it contains if it is not null, otherwise it returns the provided default value. The default value is 0.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUNIT test case generates a call to the showBug() method of the BugInOptional class. This method creates an Optional with null value using Optional.ofNullable(null). The Optional with null value is then unwrapped using the orElse(0) method, which returns the default value 0. This can lead to confusion and potential NullPointerException errors.
